Add discovery keywords to both plugin manifests (0.9.28) (#69)

The seven existing keywords all name the project or its own vocabulary,
so only someone who already knows pstack can match them. Nine terms
naming what the skills do and which runtimes they load in join the list,
including the four non-Claude runtimes the README markets.

fix(pstack): name a callable UI driver and a todolist tool on Claude Code (#73)

* fix(pstack): name a callable UI driver and a todolist tool on Claude Code

## Why

Two reports from @Graham3324. The playbooks name `verify` as the UI driver and call it a Claude Code built-in, but Claude Code's bundled `/verify` runs only when the user types it, so an agent following a playbook improvised its own driver at every UI step (#71). The todolist rule names no tool, and Claude Code 2.1.267 ships its task tools off, so a skipped playbook step left no trace (#72).

A project skill named `verify` at the repo root replaces the bundled one from Claude Code 2.1.200, and the model can call that. The generator now writes that name, and every driver line reads "`run`, or the project `verify` skill for UIs", with `run` as the fallback because it drives browser and Electron apps too. poteto-mode names `TaskCreate` and `TaskUpdate` as the todolist, the `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` switch that turns them on, and an uncommitted `todo.md` in the work dir as the fallback.

## Scope

- The driver replacement in `tools/substitutions.json`, and the same phrase in `poteto-mode/SKILL.md` and eleven playbook lines.
- `create-verification-skill` writes `.claude/skills/verify/` instead of `verify-<app>/`. `maintain-verification-skill` locates either.
- The Platform Adaptation section of `poteto-mode/SKILL.md` names the task tools and the file fallback. The README install section and `codex-tools.md` say the same.
- The README dependency note and the CHANGES substitution table stop calling `verify` a built-in the model can invoke.
- Version 0.9.29, the changelog entry, and the three manifests stamped by `tools/generate.mjs`.

## Verification

- `bun test` reports 236 pass and 0 fail after `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in `plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/scripts`.
- `bun tools/generate.mjs` stamps 0.9.29 and reports the 31 Codex prompts current. `tests/skill-collision-repro.sh` passes.
- This session's Skill tool lists `run` and not `verify`, and the session has no `TodoWrite` or `TaskCreate`, which matches both reports.

Closes #71
Closes #72

fix(poteto-mode): resolve worktree-audit trunk from the remote (0.9.33) (#81)

worktree-audit.sh named the trunk as a literal main in both its fetch and
its merge-base --is-ancestor check. On a repo that trunks anywhere else the
fetch failed, every worktree reported MERGED=?, and a fully merged worktree
never reached the safe bucket.

The script now asks the remote with git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD,
which is plumbing and needs no locale pin or placeholder match, and falls
back to main only when the remote publishes no usable HEAD. An explicit
fetch refspec updates the trunk's remote-tracking ref in a single-branch
clone. Tests run against local bare remotes for a non-main trunk, a missing
cached HEAD, a single-branch clone, and a dangling remote HEAD.

test: smoke-test Bun wrappers from caller directory (#85)

Run the shipped watch-pr and ship-pr entrypoints with --help from a foreign working directory. Nothing on main executed the extensionless wrappers, only their main() functions, so a broken import or a cwd-relative path in either one passed the suite.

One case per wrapper names the entrypoint that broke, and the child's stderr is the assertion message.

fix(poteto-mode): confirm the first Babysit status read (0.9.36) (#86)

The Babysit playbook took a PR number or status from the request and never said to check that the first status read was about that PR or stack. Step 6 now says to confirm that the PR or stack the first status read reports matches the request, and to name the current merge frontier.

The sentence adds no command. The watcher step 6 already names follows the connected open stack from one --pr and reports its frontier. Step 1 stays identical to upstream. One pin in tests/skill-rules.test.mjs holds the rule.

test: resolve fixture roots so path assertions hold on macOS (#88)

os.tmpdir() returns /var/folders/... on macOS, a symlink to /private/var/folders/.... worktree-audit.sh prints the paths git reports and resume.mjs calls realpathSync, so both emit the resolved form while the tests compared against the unresolved one. 16 tests failed on macOS and passed on Linux, where tmpdir() has no symlink in it.

Name models the way the Agent tool accepts them (0.9.40) (#93)

The Agent tool's model parameter takes opus, fable, sonnet, or haiku and rejects full IDs such as claude-opus-5-5, so every subagent's first dispatch failed. models.json now names the family names, and a test pins available to the tool's accepted set.

Model tiers and shape-based sync rules (0.9.41) (#94)

* Derive the stray-model scan from models.json available names

The scan matched only claude-* IDs, so a hard-coded family name such as `fable` passed. available is now a plain list the Agent enum test pins, and the scan builds its pattern from it.

* Name model tiers in models.json instead of inferring the strongest roles

The Codex mapping treated any single-model role off the default as the strongest tier, so a role moved to haiku was listed there. Roles now name a tier (default, strongest, panel) and the codex block uses the same keys. Stamped output is unchanged.

* Match model defaults and Cursor slugs by shape in the sync rules

The substitution table named each upstream default slug literally and the denylist listed version prefixes, so every upstream model bump needed a new rule. Rules can now carry a regex and a files scope; one pair of rules covers any vendor slug, pointing playbooks at poteto-mode's Models section and skill bodies at their own.

* Accept one lanes phrasing in check-plan and release 0.9.41

* Inline the denylist entry matching in sync.mjs

Fail CI on untracked generator output and OSV scanner errors (#96)

* Fail the generated-files job on untracked generator output

git diff --exit-code ignores untracked files, so a PR that adds a slash-command row without committing its Codex prompt passed: CI generated the prompt and the diff stayed clean.

* Propagate the OSV scanner exit code and pin its image by digest

The step ran under bash -e without pipefail, so docker run | tee returned tee's status and a scanner exit 1 on a vulnerability passed. The v2.5.1 tag is mutable; the digest matches the one CI pulled in run 35925553225.

Watch-pr: fail stale checks, reject cross-repo PR numbers and truncated stacks (#97)

* Fail completed checks that gh buckets as pending

gh pr checks puts every state it does not name in the pending bucket, including the completed conclusions STALE and STARTUP_FAILURE. The watcher waited on them forever while the GraphQL fallback already failed them. Only in-flight states now read as pending.

* Refuse the checkout's PR number for another repository

Without --pr, the number came from gh pr view in the current checkout and was paired with an explicit --owner/--repo naming a different repository, so the watcher could report READY for an unrelated PR.

* Refuse stack discovery when the open-PR list may be truncated

gh pr list --limit 300 returns the newest 300 open PRs with no truncation signal, so a stack whose bottom PR is older was cut silently and --stack could report READY with a parent PR unwatched.

Sync: carry file modes, detect binaries by content, refuse symlinks and git errors (#98)

* Remove the sync scratch clone when the denylist fails

process.exit inside the try skipped the finally, so every denylist failure left a full upstream clone under the temp dir.

* Carry upstream file modes through sync

Written files got the default mode, so an upstream 100755 script landed as 0644, and a change to the executable bit alone read as unchanged or forked.

* Detect binary sync files by content, not only extension

A .pdf or .ttf was decoded as UTF-8 and re-encoded, turning every invalid byte into EF BF BD and running substitutions over the bytes. A file with a NUL byte or bytes that do not round-trip through UTF-8 is now copied verbatim, skipped by the denylist scan, and reported as a binary conflict when it differs three ways.

* Rethrow git merge-file errors instead of counting them as hunks

Any positive status read as a conflict count, so a binary three-way diff (git exits 255) was reported as a 255-hunk conflict and the pin advanced. Git caps the conflict count at 127; anything above is an error.

* Report upstream symlinks in sync instead of following them

A file symlink copied its target's contents, from anywhere on the machine, into the port, and a directory or dangling symlink crashed the run. The deletion pass now checks the upstream entry list rather than existsSync, so a dangling link is not mistaken for a deletion.

* Refuse a dangling symlink at a portable asset target

existsSync is false for a dangling link, so the symlink guard was skipped and writeFileSync wrote through the link to a path outside the tree.

* Exclude the cursor-team-kit skills the port does not carry

The port carries 7 of the kit's 18 skills. Without an exclude list, a dry-run at the kit's own pin planned 14 added files from the other 11 and failed on their denylist hits.

* Reject slash-command text that unquoted YAML would misread

promptStub writes the reference row text unquoted into the Codex prompt's frontmatter. A ': ' made the prompt unparseable and ' #' silently truncated it, and CI passed. The generator now fails on such a row, naming the file and row, and the generated prompts stay byte-identical.

* Keep the original error when the fixture repo delete fails

An unguarded gh repo delete in finally replaced whatever error got the run there and printed no way to remove the leaked private repo. A failed delete now prints the paste-ready command and sets a failing exit code.

* Pin the strongest Codex example in the model-names test

gpt-6-astra also appears in the panel line and the negative check looked for a stale claude-opus-5 slug, so rendering the Claude strongest tier as the Codex example passed. Assert the example on the strongest line and forbid every Claude family name in the section.

* Strip every stamped region before checking role labels in prose

The test stripped only the Models section, but the generator also stamps a Model names section into poteto-mode's codex-tools.md that lists the strongest-tier labels, so deleting a label from the SKILL.md prose stayed green.

* Remove sync and invariants test fixtures after each test

Both files created fixture trees with mkdtempSync and never removed them, leaving 88 directories in the temp dir per run.

* Name the script list once in the sync mode test

Fix edge cases in worktree-audit, check-plan, find-transcript, and log.sh (#99)

* Resolve the worktree-audit script path from the test file

* Make worktree-audit stubs honour the gh, jq, and rg arguments

The gh, jq, and rg stubs ignored their arguments, so dropping --state all, breaking the jq filter, or loosening the rg pattern left every test green. gh now rejects a call without --state all, jq is the real binary (ubuntu-latest ships it), and rg delegates to grep -r so the pattern decides the match.

* Fix worktree-audit marking a chatted worktree safe

rg honoured .gitignore, the global excludes file, and user rg config, so a transcript under an ignoring repo never matched; a missing transcripts dir was skipped silently. Either way a clean, merged worktree with a live chat came out safe. Search with --no-config -uu and downgrade to review when the transcripts dir is absent.

* Fix check-plan linting fences nested in list items as prose

Fence detection allowed at most three spaces of indent, so a fence under a list item (four spaces) was linted as prose and a valid plan failed with a mid-sentence colon inside the code.

* Exercise find-transcript's malformed-line guard and clean up fixtures

The truncated line sat after the user record, where openingPrompt had already returned, so a bare JSON.parse passed every test. Put it before any user record in the newest candidate, and remove each temp dir after its test.

* Fix find-transcript doing nothing under node via a symlinked path

node resolves import.meta.url through symlinks but leaves argv[1] as typed, so the main guard never matched: no output and exit 0 on both hit and miss. Compare against the resolved argv[1].

* Fix log.sh letting a leading quote reshape the decision log

A quote-aware TSV reader unwraps a cell that opens with " (turning "=HYPERLINK(...)" into a formula) and runs an unterminated one into later rows. Prefix those cells with a single quote like the formula characters.

* Run merge-safety.md's restack block in the shipping git tests

The tests hand-copied the recipe, so editing the doc (a bare --force-with-lease, a rebase without --onto) could not fail them. Extract the sh block and execute it with its variables bound.

* Report claude's exit status and output when the collision repro fails

Under set -e a failing claude call exited the script before the FAIL line, hiding claude's stderr.

* Name the leading quote in show-me-your-work's log.sh description

* Keep find-transcript importable under node when argv[1] is not a file

realpathSync threw ENOENT at import time for node -e ... arg, which the symlink fix introduced.

* Name the node probe and the risky log cells in their tests

Watcher check states and script edge cases (0.9.42) (#100)

watch-pr stops at the review gate (0.9.43) (#95)

* watch-pr waits on the review gate (0.9.42)

watch-pr reported READY for a PR held by a required approval: the
readiness proof ignored REVIEW_REQUIRED and accepted a BLOCKED merge
state when the head rollup was not failing. Such a PR now waits on a
review reason and times out with exit 5.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Report the review gate as a merge-gate blocker (0.9.43)

A required review or a BLOCKED merge state now ends in the terminal merge-gate blocker (exit 6) instead of a WAITING that runs until the deadline, which is forever under --timeout 0. The shipping playbook routes human approval gates to its own wait. Both gates defer while checks are pending. 0.9.42 shipped in #100, so this release is 0.9.43.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Michael Denyer <michael.denyer@effem.com>

Reasoning effort per role through effort agents (0.9.44) (#101)

* Reasoning effort per role through effort agents

Rebased from #90 onto 0.9.43 by keeping main's model tiers and family names, and adding the efforts list beside them.

* Effort agents for every dispatch type, owned-file cleanup (0.9.44)

The Reasoning effort rule picks the agent from the subagent_type the caller would otherwise use, so arena and architect, which name none, get pstack:effort-<level> alone and pstack:poteto-agent-<level> under poteto-mode. The generator lists the agents it wrote in tools/effort-agents.json and removes or overwrites only those. Effort examples use family names, and the effort agent's description says it is a custom agent rather than the built-in general-purpose one.

* Default reasoning effort of medium, set by the sheet's default effort line

A role value without @level now dispatches through the effort agent for models.json defaultEffort (medium). The override sheet's default effort line changes it, and default effort: session keeps the parent session's effort.

* Default effort falls back to the session's

defaultEffort is session, so a role value without @level keeps the parent session's effort as in #90. The sheet's default effort line still sets a level for every such role.

* Refuse non-regular effort agent paths, resolve aliases and Codex effort

syncEffortAgents rejects a symlink or directory at any path it would write or remove, before changing anything. The stamped effort rule strips the suffix before reading the model, so inherit-parent @high still omits model, and names Codex's spawn_agent reasoning_effort beside the Claude Code agents.

* Give effort agents a directory the generator owns

The effort agents move to plugins/pstack/effort-agents/, which the generator owns outright like the portable asset directories, so tools/effort-agents.json and its symlink and missing-manifest cases go away. plugin.json's stamped agents list names every file in both directories, because a custom list replaces the default agents/ directory.

The SessionStart hook and setup-pstack honour CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Shared skills name the sheet as pstack-models.md; setup-pstack's runtime table and the hook own the path. Fixes #102. Contributed by @gordon-marx-included.

Add pstack plugin icon (#107)

* Add pstack plugin icon

* Declare Claude plugin icon for directory submission

Resolve plugin directory submission holds (0.9.46) (#108)

The directory validator held the submission on the SessionStart hook, which resolved its mandate file through a dirname expression a static reader cannot follow, and on the eval playbook, whose backticked eval keyword read as a shell execute pattern. The hook now names its file through CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and carries a .sh extension so CI lints it; the playbook lists its blinding words as plain text.

Add directory listing metadata and a plugin-root README (0.9.47) (#109)

The plugin directory reads documentationUrl, supportUrl, privacyPolicyUrl, and termsOfServiceUrl from plugin.json and shows the plugin folder's README as the listing; neither existed. The repository README's Data handling section now names what each script and the hook reads or calls, so the directory's disclosure scan has something to compare against.

Report a READY observation that completes at the watch deadline (#110)

The post-step expiry check in pollUntilTerminal ran before the terminal check and before a sleep result assigned its onDeadline, so a complete READY became a generic TIMEOUT and the pending-checks or queued-stack timeout reason was lost. The loop-top check already covers expiry.

Pass the runtime to the session hook and give the sheet path one home (#112)

Each runtime's hooks file now names its runtime, so the hook no longer guesses from PLUGIN_ROOT, a generic variable a Claude Code session can inherit. setup-pstack names the Codex directory <codex-home> and the other docs link to its runtime table, so with CODEX_HOME set it writes the sheet the hook reads.

Model the watch-pr merge gate, revision, and deadline explicitly (#124)

* Make the merge-gate hint exhaustive over MergeGateReason

The hint was a ternary whose final else printed the changes-requested text, so a new gate reason would have printed the wrong action. Pin the gate decision and every hint first.

* Carry the landing revision in open PullRequestFacts

parsePullRequest validated an open PR's head and base commits and discarded the result, so readSnapshot checked them again and spread them back in. PullRequestFacts is now a union on state whose OPEN arm is a LandingRevision, built where the response is parsed. The fake reader goes through the same parser.

* Require one WatchDeadline and end polling at the loop condition

The deadline was optional in the reader, the CLI runtime, and the poll loop, and each layer built its own fallback, so a caller could run the reader and the loop on two budgets. CliRuntime, RunDependencies, GhGitHubReader, run, and runJson now take the one deadline realRuntime builds, and StepResult.onDeadline is required.

The loop condition is the only clock check. A command cancelled at the deadline leaves through the same return and is not retried. A read that fails past the deadline now takes the ordinary failure path. It reports the status-query blocker when it uses up --max-query-errors, and otherwise emits one RETRY of 0 seconds before the same TIMEOUT.

classify read old, new, and local through boolean read flags that had to mirror its early returns.
